seo.title: Features – HubGet
seo.description: One app = one card. When an app is available from several package managers, its card shows every source and you choose where to install from.
seo.ogDescription: One app = one card. When an app is available from several package managers, its card shows every source and you choose where to install from.

texty.t2: The store you know from your phone. Built for Windows.
texty.t3: One app = one card. When an app is available from several package managers, its card shows every source and you choose where to install from.
texty.t5: A “Today” home page with tips from hundreds of well-known apps, category picks and a new App of the Day every day, categories, charts and collections by profession. Quick search with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> covers the catalog and searches package managers live.
texty.t6: 25,000+ apps from WinGet, Chocolatey and Scoop
texty.t7: Collections by profession and top charts
texty.t8: “Regular user” mode shows desktop apps only
texty.t10: App pages like the App Store
texty.t11: A large banner whose color adapts to the app’s icon. A screenshot gallery with a full-screen viewer, what’s new, privacy details and quick links to the website, GitHub, documentation and support.
texty.t12: Technical details: SHA-256, installer type, system requirements, dependencies
texty.t13: Every source of the app on a single card
texty.t16: An overview of every app on your PC – including programs installed outside WinGet, Microsoft Store apps and Steam games. Install all available updates with a single “Update all” button.
texty.t17: Uninstall, and an Open button to launch the app
texty.t18: Operation queue and download progress in percent
texty.t19: Ignore updates or postpone them for a day, a week or a month
texty.t20: If an operation fails due to permissions, HubGet retries it as administrator
texty.t23: Uninstallers often leave settings, caches, shortcuts and registry keys behind. After an uninstall, HubGet finds them – in AppData, Program Files and ProgramData, the Start menu, on the desktop and in the Windows registry – and offers to delete them. Or it cleans them up right away and just lets you know.
texty.t24: With **install monitoring**, HubGet takes a disk and registry snapshot before and after an install. It remembers what the installer created and offers to remove all of it after an uninstall – even items it couldn’t find by name.
texty.t25: Files go to the Recycle Bin; registry keys are backed up before they’re deleted
texty.t26: Never deletes anything that belongs to another installed app
texty.t27: Closes the running app before the uninstall
texty.t28: Off by default – turn it on in Settings
texty.t42: Registry keys are saved to a backup (.reg) before they’re deleted.
texty.t46: What starts as soon as you sign in to Windows? HubGet shows programs from the registry, the Startup folder, Task Scheduler and Store apps in one place – with their name, publisher and icon.
texty.t47: Enable and disable in one click, just like in Task Manager
texty.t48: Startup impact: high, medium, low – from Windows’ own measurement
texty.t49: Remove for good, with a backup – including leftovers of uninstalled programs
texty.t73: A disabled program won’t start but stays in the list.
texty.t75: Before you install an app, see how others rate it. Every app shows its star average, the rating breakdown and the most helpful reviews – sign in with GitHub to add your own.
texty.t76: Stars and reviews under the name from your GitHub account
texty.t77: Edit or delete your own review any time, report inappropriate ones
texty.t78: Signing in is optional – everything else works without an account
texty.t90: Installs and updates everything in one place. Exactly what I was looking for.
texty.t94: As administrator, interactively, a specific (even older) version, architecture, scope, custom arguments – or just download the installer.
texty.t96: Build your own shareable bundle of apps – a new PC set up in five minutes. Your profile with its settings as JSON or a readable HTML page, a WinGet export, favorites.
texty.t98: A custom Windows 11-style title bar, smooth animations and instant page transitions. Light and dark theme that follows Windows. A welcome tour shows you around on first launch.
texty.t100: Operation history and logs, clearing package manager caches. In seven languages: English, Czech, German, Spanish, French, Portuguese and Chinese.
texty.t102: Signed-in users add current screenshots to apps. HubGet downscales them to WebP without metadata, and everyone sees them once approved. Anything inappropriate can be reported.
texty.t104: Favorites, your package bundle and preferences on all your computers. Signing in is optional – everything else works without an account.
texty.t106: Close the window. Installs keep going.
texty.t107: Closing the window tucks HubGet away into the notification area next to the clock, where running installs finish quietly. The transparent monochrome icon adapts to light and dark taskbars, and its tooltip shows how many updates are available.
